Forecast Discussion

High pressure over the Northeast keeps a dry wedge against the east side of the Appalachians today. The air is cool but not unusual for late October, and sunshine builds back this morning. The high settles overhead Monday, so the wedge erodes and afternoons warm Monday and Tuesday. Clear, calm nights bring frost to the valleys.

Another high builds over New England Wednesday. An easterly flow adds clouds and a nudge of cooler air for a day. Somewhat warmer air returns Thursday and Friday.

Clouds thicken Saturday ahead of a system moving in from the west. Rain probably waits until next Sunday, but I put a mention in the late Saturday night forecast just in case. I think trick-or-treating remains dry, but we will be watching that point.
